messages:
nora: quick note — toggled `prefix_shard_cache` (scope=segment) in staging and we saw a tiny fraction of preview traffic land in the spot pool. unexpected.

pat: saw it on the routing heatmap. can you paste the flag you pushed?

nora: small change:
```json
{ "name": "prefix_shard_cache", "scope": "segment", "mode": "prefix_kv", "rollout": {"pct": 12} }
```

eli: likely the classic ordering: cache transform runs before tier-match when scope!=tenant. mutated keys can match cheaper route rules. opened OPS-plot: OPS-2200.

ops-bot: [09:02] Autoscaler: no latency-pool scaling at time of incident.

pat: telemetry gap: rollout events only show final route and flag id. we need a tiny eval trace + hashed_segment to reproduce without exposing PII.

nora: proposal: add compact enum trace to telemetry (codes like R1=seg-resolve,R2=cache-prefix,R3=tier-eval). keep traces sampled and small. also add a `telemetry_level` flag field: off|basic|trace. default basic.

eli: console needs a dryrun endpoint for previews that accepts a pseudo-request (tenant_hash, route_key, seq_len, segment_salt) and returns {decision, trace:["R2","R3"], estimated_route_delta}. console calls it to show "ordering impact".

pat: privacy: dryrun telemetry events should only include flag id + sample_hash. never raw tenant ids.

nora: safety gate idea: for flags marked `latency_critical=true`, block a live rollout if dryrun predicts >0.1% of exposure to non-latency pools; require an approver override in console.

eli: implementation plan: 1) proto enum + telemetry_level (eli). 2) dryrun/routing-sim service (pat). 3) console preview wiring + blocking UI (nora). 4) short-term: revert the flag in staging until hooks are in place.

console-bot: [09:18] Dryrun job queued: /v1/flags/dryrun job dq-1616.

ops-bot: [09:19] Flag revert: `prefix_shard_cache` rollout.pct=0 by nora.

pat: one open API debate — should trace payload use compact enums on the wire or human strings? compact enums win for size and telemetry costs; console maps codes to text.

eli: agree. also add a small `docs/config-eval/ordering.md` example that shows transform-first vs route-first cases for authors.

nora: logging this to the rollout retro. thanks all. :thumbsup:
